title: How are gas market developments reshaping US power markets?
gist: Wood Mackenzie promotional teaser for an infographic arguing US gas and power markets are becoming tightly interconnected: data-centre-driven electricity demand growth is turning power into a bigger gas-demand driver while LNG exports compete for the same supply. It lists five gas-market developments (power demand, LNG competition, pipelines, regional dynamics, oil/geopolitics) but gives no data.

themes.theme: Power demand as gas demand driver

insights.claim: After years of relatively flat US electricity demand, data centres and other large loads are accelerating power demand, making the power sector a growing driver of US natural gas demand.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Data-centre load growth is a structural bid for US gas-fired generation and the gas that feeds it; watch gas-burn data alongside load forecasts.
insights.quote: After years of relatively flat electricity demand, data centres and other large loads are accelerating power demand
insights.locator: Why do gas markets matter for power market planning?

insights.claim: Assessing the US power outlook increasingly requires analysing gas fuel availability, pipeline infrastructure, LNG demand and regional gas dynamics, because these determine where gas-fired generation is viable and how its economics develop.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Power-asset siting and valuation should be stress-tested against regional gas deliverability, not just electricity demand.
insights.quote: understanding the power outlook increasingly means looking beyond the electricity market itself
insights.locator: For utilities, developers and other power-market participants

insights.claim: Growing US LNG exports and changing regional gas flows are creating additional competition for gas supply that power generators also depend on.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Rising LNG feedgas plus rising power burn tightens US gas balances; supportive for gas prices and producers, a cost risk for gas-fired generators.
insights.locator: Why do gas markets matter for power market planning?

insights.claim: Pipeline development determines where gas can physically move, and regional gas dynamics can affect both gas-fired generation and where load growth can be served.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Pipeline bottlenecks create regional winners and losers; track pipeline projects in data-centre growth regions.
insights.locator: Our new infographic explores five gas-market developments

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie argues oil markets and geopolitics can still influence the US power-market picture via their effect on gas markets.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Oil/geopolitical shocks can transmit to US power prices through gas; keep cross-commodity exposure in risk models.
insights.quote: Why oil markets and geopolitics can still influence the power-market picture
insights.locator: Our new infographic explores five gas-market developments
